title: AMD's AI Hardware and Software Ecosystem: Driving the Future of Agentic and Physical AI
description: This presentation details AMD's comprehensive strategy, covering high-performance hardware like the MI350P and EPYC Venice, architectural innovations like Triplet computing, and the software ecosystem (ROCm, Rockum.AI). It concludes by outlining the shift toward agentic AI and embodied AI robotics to redefine human-machine interaction.
summary: The presentation covers the capabilities and strategic importance of AMD's AI hardware, detailing the performance of the MI350P and EPYC Venice processors, which deliver significantly higher performance per watt (up to 3.3x) and massive compute capacity for enterprise workloads. The discussion emphasizes AMD's Triplet Innovation and the power of the ROCm software stack, noting how tools like Rockum.AI simplify model optimization and accelerate development for AI agents. Finally, the presentation pivots to the future of AI, arguing that agentic AI and empathetic AI—AI that can act in the physical world—represent the next major transition, supported by new robotics platforms like the Kria AI Developer Platform.

title: The Evolution of AI Compute: From Data Centers to Pervasive Intelligence
description: This discussion explores the accelerating growth of AI, the critical need for scalable compute infrastructure, and the shift toward a distributed, pervasive AI future that integrates into enterprise, personal, and physical realities.
summary: The speakers discussed the rapid evolution of AI capabilities, highlighting the move from basic chatbots to complex agents and the corresponding exponential growth in compute demand. Key strategies include building broad compute engines, fostering open platforms, and focusing on the recursive improvement of AI systems. The discussion covered the challenges of deploying AI in enterprise settings (power, cooling, integration) and the shift towards a distributed model. Furthermore, they outlined the future of AI, which moves beyond the data center and screen into personal AI and physical AI (robotics), where agents sense, navigate, and act in the real world. The ultimate vision is an ecosystem where compute connects all forms of intelligence across silicon and software.

title: The Future of Enterprise AI: Hardware, Open Source Strategy, and Operational Efficiency
description: This discussion covers the advancements in AI infrastructure (like the Venice server family), the strategic importance of the open-source ecosystem, and the key enterprise challenges related to managing costs, security, and agent behavior at scale.
summary: The speaker discusses the evolution of AI infrastructure, introducing the Venice server family built on the Zen 6 core, designed for the agentic era, emphasizing performance, efficiency, and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO). The strategy relies on leveraging the x86 architecture for compatibility while simultaneously driving down costs through intelligent routing and abstraction. Partnerships with the open-source ecosystem are crucial for achieving velocity and scale. Enterprise adoption is accelerating, driven by a demand for agentic deployments, and efforts are focused on managing token costs and scaling usage across diverse enterprise workloads. Crucially, the discussion stresses the need for robust governance, including ensuring sufficient network bandwidth, containing token consumption, and monitoring agent behavior for safety and security, all managed through a unified control plane. The final takeaway is the availability of comprehensive management tools (like Halo) to provide full visibility and control over the entire AI estate.

title: AMD's Strategy for the AI Ecosystem: Open Hardware, Agentic Software, and AI Everywhere
description: This presentation outlines AMD's strategy to position itself at the forefront of AI computing by combining open hardware standards with advanced agentic software solutions. It highlights new tools like Rockum.AI and the Crea AI system, demonstrating how AI can dramatically accelerate development and expand market reach across enterprise, cloud, and sovereign AI.
summary: This session focused on AMD's mission to push the boundaries of high-performance and AI computing, driven by the belief that AI is a force multiplier for market growth. Key points included the necessity of an open ecosystem (hardware and software) to service the projected massive market for high-performance computing. The speaker introduced Rockum.AI, an agentic platform designed to help developers use AI coding agents to build and optimize workloads on the AMD ecosystem, leveraging AI to generate high-quality GPU kernels. The strategy emphasizes leveraging open-source models, including a groundbreaking achievement where AMD was the first telecom company to train a model on their hardware, and the release of the OTel 2.0 open-source model. Finally, the introduction of the AMD Crea AI system, powered by Ryzen AI embedded technology, showcased a holistic approach to AI compute across various platforms, demonstrating the next phase of AI where tools are provided to make AI give AI the opportunity to deliver real-world impact.

title: Co-designing the Future of AI Hardware and Ecosystem Partnerships
description: This discussion focuses on the critical need for deep hardware-software co-design, strategic partnerships, and building a secure, flexible ecosystem for scaling AI infrastructure. It emphasizes how collaborative efforts in hardware and software development are essential for future AI capabilities.
summary: The conversation centered on the importance of strategic partnerships and collaboration in advancing AI infrastructure. One speaker highlighted the effort involved in developing new hardware platforms, noting that the journey from initial prototyping (like the MI355 evaluation) to full deployment requires integrated work across hardware design, layout, and adjacent software engineering. They stressed that co-designing power and cooling today will unlock vastly superior performance in future systems (2027-2028). The other speaker emphasized the success of a partnership, referencing the deployment of massive AMD infrastructure (MI455) and the seamless collaboration between hardware and software teams, which provides unique insights into future workload needs. They stressed that the opportunity lies in leveraging AI not just for model deployment, but for training models and managing enterprise workloads across the entire infrastructure, while ensuring robust safety and security for the entire apparatus. Ultimately, the speakers agreed that a full-stack approach, combining hardware, software, and ecosystem efforts, is necessary to build the future.

title: Co-designing the Future of AI: Integrated Data Centers and the AMD Partnership
description: This discussion focuses on the necessity of co-designing entire data centers—including CPUs, GPUs, networking, power, and cooling—to maximize performance. It highlights a strategic partnership with AMD and the introduction of Cerebrus, a new chip architecture designed to deliver ultra-low latency solutions.
summary:
The speaker emphasizes the need to move beyond optimizing individual components (like a single CPU) to co-designing the entire data center ecosystem—considering servers, hardware, networking, cooling, and power as an integrated system. This holistic approach is crucial as compute demands evolve toward agentic workloads. The speaker highlights the strategic importance of collaborating with partners like AMD, recognizing that CPUs are becoming as critical as GPUs in the evolving AI landscape.

Key technical and strategic points include:
*   **System-Level Thinking:** Designing the data center as a unified system where all components must work together, rather than optimizing hardware in isolation.
*   **CPU/GPU Co-design:** Recognizing that CPUs and GPUs are becoming conjoined systems, and workloads should dictate the right hardware combination.
*   **Memory Bandwidth and Tuning:** The importance of memory bandwidth and the ability for customers to independently tune different components based on their specific workload requirements.
*   **Cerebrus Partnership:** Announcing a partnership with Cerebrus to build a disaggregated solution combining AMD CPUs, SRAM, and memory bandwidth to deliver an unmatched, ultra-low latency system. This new solution will be offered via the Cerebrus cloud and eventually in retail stores.
*   **Software and Data Sovereignty:** Stressing that hardware is only part of the story; software and developer platforms are essential. The concept of data sovereignty—not being tied to a specific chipset—is key, allowing computing capacity to scale across edge devices and PCs, thus reducing strain on data centers and lowering overall infrastructure costs.

title: The Leadership of Epic and Venius in Data Center Computing
description: This overview discusses the comprehensive Epic CPU portfolio, highlighting its architectural breadth and its superior performance, density, and power efficiency across both general-purpose and specialized AI/agentic workloads.
summary:
The presentation introduced the Epic processor lineup, emphasizing its design for high-density performance, scalability, and efficiency across diverse workloads. Epic is positioned as the best server CPU due to its architecture, which spans dozens of chip types, offering unparalleled flexibility and optimization for enterprise applications.

Key performance metrics and advantages include:
*   **Overall Leadership:** The fifth-generation Epic Turn is highlighted as a top-tier server CPU, featuring up to 192 cores and 384 threads, built on a 2nm process, providing superior performance per dollar.
*   **Workload Specialization:** The CPU portfolio is tailored for different needs: high-frequency cores and fast I/O for GPU servers (driving GPUs), and efficiency and diversity for general-purpose enterprise applications (databases, services).
*   **AI and Agentic Performance:** The Venius architecture excels in AI workloads, delivering 1.8 times more tokens per second than competitive x86 processors and delivering more than twice the performance per watt for agent sandboxes.
*   **Competitive Edge:** Venius maintains a significant lead over competing ARM CPUs, delivering 20% higher per-core performance and 2.2 times more performance at the socket level when paired with core density.
*   **Flexibility and Portfolio:** To meet diverse enterprise demands, the Epic portfolio offers a wide range of SKUs (8 to 13 architectures) with varying core counts, power, and I/O capabilities, ensuring customers can select the most optimized solution for their specific workload.

title: The Exponential Acceleration of AI Demand: Tokens, Training, and the Rise of Agentic AI
description: This discussion highlights the massive, exponential growth in AI demand, driven by a 158x increase in token consumption and scaling model training compute. It focuses on how agentic AI is shifting the infrastructure demand, creating a significant new market for server CPUs.
summary: The video illustrates the accelerating demand for AI, noting a staggering 158x increase in tokens consumed per month over the last two years, and training compute (FLOPS) increasing 5x yearly since 2020. This exponential demand is fueled by the shift from merely building models to deploying them through agentic AI, which is accelerating rapidly. The AI accelerator market is projected to reach $1.4 trillion by 2030. A key finding is that agentic AI is creating a new growth vector for server CPUs, leading to a forecast for the server CPU market to grow from $25 billion to over $200 billion by 2030. The discussion emphasizes that the infrastructure for agentic AI requires distributed platforms, necessitating high performance across various components, and highlights the exponential demand across all AI applications, including inference, training, and content creation.
